text: The predominant intermolecular forces present in ethyl acetate, a liquid, are:
options: London dispersion, dipole-dipole and hydrogen bonding
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Ethyl acetate $(CH_{3}$COOCH$_{2}CH_{3})$ is an organic compound with a molecular structure that does not include any hydrogen atoms bonded directly to highly electronegative atoms like nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine. Because of this, it cannot form hydrogen bonds. However, ethyl acetate does possess a polar carbonyl group (C=O), which contributes to dipole-dipole interactions, and like all molecules, it can experience London dispersion forces. Therefore, the predominant intermolecular forces present in ethyl acetate are dipole-dipole interactions and London dispersion forces.

Hence, the correct option is :

Option D: London dispersion and dipole-dipole
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot

text:
The rate of a certain biochemical reaction at physiological temperature (T) occurs $10^{6}$ times faster with
enzyme than without. The change in the activation energy upon adding enzyme is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The rate constant of a reaction without catalyst is

$k=Ae^{-\frac{Ea}{RT}}$

The rate constant in presence of catalyst is
given by

$k^{'}=Ae^{-\frac{E'a}{RT}}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{k^{'}}{k}=e^{-\frac{\left (E'a-Ea\right )}{RT}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $10^{6} =$ $e^{-\frac{\left (E'a-Ea\right )}{RT}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\ln  10^{6} =$ $-\frac{(E{}_{a}^{'}-E_{a})}{RT}$

$\Rightarrow$ $E{}_{a}^{'}-E_{a}$ = -RTln $10^{6}$

$\Rightarrow$ $E{}_{a}^{'}-E_{a}$ = -6RT$\times$2.303
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot

text:
For the Balmer series in the spectrum of H atom,

$ν–=R_{H}\left \{\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right \}$, the correct statements among (I) to (IV)
are :

(I) As wavelength decreases, the lines in the series converge

(II) The integer $n_{1}$ is equal to 2

(III) The line of longest wavelength corresponds to $n_{2} = 3$

(IV) The ionization energy of hydrogen can be calculated from wave number of these lines
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the Balmer series the electron falls to $n_{1}=2$ from $n_{2}=3,4,5,\ldots$, so (II) is correct.

The longest wavelength has the smallest wave number, from the smallest jump $n_{2}=3$: $\bar{ν}=R_{H}\left (\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{9}\right )=\dfrac{5R_{H}}{36}$, so (III) is correct.

As $n_{2}$ increases, $\bar{ν}$ approaches the limit $\dfrac{R_{H}}{4}$ and successive lines crowd together, so the lines converge as the wavelength decreases; (I) is correct.

The series limit $\dfrac{R_{H}}{4}$ corresponds to removing the electron from $n=2$, not from the ground state $n=1$ (which needs $R_{H}$), so the ionization energy of hydrogen does not follow from Balmer wave numbers; (IV) is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot

text:
The magnitude of work done by a gas that undergoes a reversible expansion along the path ABC shown in
the figure is $_______$.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The axes in the figure meet at $V=2\text{m}^{3}$, $P=2\text{Pa}$, so the work $W=\int PdV$ is the area between path ABC and the line $P=0$.

Along AB the pressure is constant at $8\text{Pa}$ while the volume rises from $2$ to $8\text{m}^{3}$:

$W_{AB}=8\times (8-2)=48\text{J}$

Along BC the pressure falls linearly from $8$ to $2\text{Pa}$ while the volume rises from $8$ to $12\text{m}^{3}$, so the area is a trapezium:

$W_{BC}=\dfrac{1}{2}(8+2)\times (12-8)=20\text{J}$

$|W|=W_{AB}+W_{BC}=48+20=68\text{J}$

Hence, the answer is 68.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot

text:
Ferrous sulphate heptahydrate is used to fortify foods with iron. The amount (in grams) of the salt required to
achieve 10 ppm of iron in 100 kg of wheat is $_______$.

Atomic weight : Fe = 55.85; S = 32.00;
O = 16.00
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 8th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
FeSO$_{4}.7H_{2}O (M = 277.85)$

PPM = 
     Mass of Iron
     Mass of wheat
 $\times$ $10^{6}$

$\Rightarrow$ 10 = 
     Mass of Iron
     100 $\times$ $10^{3}$
$\times$ $10^{6}$

$\Rightarrow$ Mass of Iron = 1 gm

Molecular mass of FeSO$_{4}.7H_{2}O$ is 277.85

55.85 gm iron is present in 277.85 gm of salt

1 gm iron is present in = $\frac{277.85}{55.85}$ = 4.97 gm of salt.
